title: How do we read births from a monthly line graph?
description: A line graph shows the number of births in every month in India. The video reads one month, finds the time period, compares three Januaries and estimates the births in a whole year, saying about for every reading.
teaching_notes: One idea: each dot is one month, so a year needs twelve readings, and every reading is about a number. Watch for students who read one dot as the whole year.

source: Figure it Out (visualising data, question 2 of the second set)
video_script.why: The child can read one dot of the space graph but has not yet used a long monthly line to compare months and estimate a year.
video_script.substitution: Go up from the month to the line and across to the scale, say about, and add twelve monthly readings for a year.
video_script.anchor: the book's line graph of the number of births in every month in India
video_script.payoff_line: each answer is read from the graph and given as about a number

final_answer.value: Answers are read off the graph and given as approximate values
final_answer.spoken: each answer is read from the graph and given as about a number

never_show: an exact number read from the graph
maths_rules: no data values are fixed here: every answer is read off the graph and given as about a number
(i) say what the line does: where it is highest and lowest, and how it rises and falls
(ii) go up from July 2017 to the line, then across to the side scale
(iii) the time period runs from the first labelled month to the last labelled month on the bottom axis
(iv) read the three January dots (2018, 2019, 2020) and compare their heights; the highest dot is the most births
(v) births in 2019 = the sum of the 12 monthly readings, or a typical month x 12 as a quick estimate
slip: one dot is one month, so one dot is not the births in a year
video_script.design: One idea: read each dot as one month and say about. The wrong idea is that one dot is a whole year. The graph stays on screen all video; no data values are invented.
open_questions: The graph values are not in the extracted book text, so no reading can be checked; the video gives the method and says about for every reading.
